title: soft liftoff tactics and escort cohort checklist
content:
Context:
Personal scratchpad for a "soft liftoff" release pattern that escort-cohorts the new model/version through progressively larger client slices while maintaining conservative safety/fallbacks. Aim: minimal blast radius, smooth warmup of caches and KV, and clear escape hatches for fast rollback or pinback.

High-level approach (one-liner):
- Start with tiny stealth cohort (0.05-0.2%) -> escort cohorts (0.5%, 2%, 8%, 25%) -> broad ramp if SLOs pass. Each step includes warmup, telemetry gating, and a 30–90m observation window.

Quick checklist (pre-roll):
- [ ] Create release ticket and add exec summary + risks (INF-879).
- [ ] Confirm model artifact SHA and full provenance (weights, quantization profile).
- [ ] Pin variant IDs for fallback (v1-stable -> v2-candidate; fallback route preconfigured).
- [ ] Reserve a burst pool for warmup traffic (dedicated capacity or simulated warm traffic).
- [ ] Determine escort cohorts: list of client buckets (see "escort list" below).
- [ ] Add SDK flag toggle + server-side router flag for immediate pinback.
- [ ] Smoke-run canaries in staging with identical config.
- [ ] Validate observability: dashboards, alerts, and synthetic checks.
- [ ] Postmortem template pre-attached to ticket.

Escort cohort sequencing (practical):
1) Stealth probe (0.05% global) — 15–30 min window
  - Use low-risk tenants (internal test tenants, known stable partners)
  - Verify p95 latency, error rate < 0.1%, token cost within expected bounds
  - Verify hallucination/regression checks on sampled prompts (eval harness)
2) Micro escort (0.5%) — 30–60 min
  - Add 3 small external clients grouped by non-critical flows
  - Watch model-specific metrics: repetition rate, truncated responses, undesired stop tokens
3) Escort alpha (2%) — 60–90 min
  - Warm KV cache: prefill using representative prefixes for heavy clients
  - Enable continuous batching; monitor batch sizes and tail latency
4) Escort beta (8%) — 90–180 min
  - Observe cost delta per-1000 tokens; ensure within budget thresholds
5) Broad ramp candidate (25%) -> broad (50%/100%) conditional on gate success

Warmup and priming notes:
- Warmup tokens: push synthetic requests matching top 20 client prompt shapes. Target ~5–10M warmup tokens per GPU pool before 2% step.
- KV pre-warm: use replay of recent traffic sans PII; scrubbed traces.
- Model cache TTLs: set initial short TTLs (5–10m) during first escort then extend once stable.

Telemetry gates (must be green to advance):
- Latency: p95 < target_p95 * 1.15 and p99 < target_p99 * 1.25
- Error rate: overall request failures < 0.2% and model fallback events < 0.05%
- QoQ hallucination/regression: sample-eval metric (BLEU/ROUGE style for structured outputs) within delta threshold (config per eval suite)
- Cost/throughput: per-token compute cost delta <= 30% relative to baseline OR justified by quality gains
- Observed divergence in token distribution / truncation events flagged -> pause and investigate

Escape hatches and rollback triggers:
- Immediate pinback: flip router flag to v1-stable (zero-downtime reroute)
- Partial siphon: move high-risk client cohorts back to v1 while keeping others on v2 for continued analysis
- Circuit-breaker thresholds (auto action): p99 latency > 2x or error rate increase > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes -> auto-throttle to 10% traffic and page oncall
- If data-exfil/hallucination spike observed, isolate model and start forensics, enable stricter content filters

Operational playbook snippets (commands and quick ops):
- Router toggle (example): curl -X POST $ROUTER/admin/switch -d '{"route":"model:v2-candidate","percent":0.5}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Pinback (fast): nav to console -> routes -> select route -> rollback -> choose v1-stable -> confirm (auto-redirect is tested)
- Warmup script (pseudo): python tools/warmup.py --clients clients-list.csv --tokens 5000000 --parallel 8 --scrub true

Client cohort selection heuristics:
- Prefer clients with low-fatality flows (search, metadata enrichment) for early escorts
- Avoid high-value billing flows or legal/regulatory flows (e.g., billing reconciliation, legal assist) in first 3 cohorts
- Prefer clients whose prompts match the model's training distribution for faster stability

Data and privacy notes:
- Warmup/replay must be scrubbed of PII; use hashed client IDs and remove verbatim user content unless consent/TOU permits.
- For private deployments, coordinate with customer-managed KMS before any warmup artifacts leave the VPC

Observation logging template (what to capture each step):
- step_name: window_start/window_end
- cohort_list: names
- traffic%: numeric
- p95/p99 latency, errors, fallback_count, batch_size distribution
- sampled outputs: 10 positive / 10 suspicious examples with notes
- operator_notes: free text

Post-rollout followups (first 72h):
- 6h check-in: confirm metric trends remain stable and no silent regressions
- 24h: run extended eval set and rebaseline quality metrics
- 48–72h: revisit cost vs quality; document if quantization or kernel changes needed

Open questions / TODOs for next pass:
- Determine automatic warmup budget per tenant (formula: tokens proportional to daily QPS percentile)
- Add a lightweight smoke-sample that runs a mini-eval on ~1k real-world queries every 15m
- Clarify SLO multipliers for holiday traffic (higher tolerance windows?)
- Bake in a synthetic-slowdown test to detect adverse perf under heavy tail batching

Notes to self:
- Keep the first 2 escorts to business hours of a major region to ensure pager coverage
- Make sure runbook links are embedded in the ticket and on Slack #deploys before flip
- Practice the pinback with the SRE runbook in staging at least twice before production

Recent small experiments that informed this draft:
- 2024-09 micro-escort on partner X: KV warmup reduced p95 by 18% after 45m
- 2024-10 stealth probe: detected subtle truncation issue caused by new tokenization; fixed by kernel switch

End.
